findings.evidence: Page 130 Table 5-1 note: "Note: 2 × params × L treats the token-embedding table as a per-position matmul; it is a lookup, so the proxy overstates compute — most for the smallest model (MiniLM’s table is ~51% of its params). Body-parameter ratios are the truer cross-model comparison (mpnet/MiniLM ≈7.7× body-only vs 4.8× by total params ...), so the proxy overstates each model’s compute most for the smallest, and the proxy ratio (4.8×) is a lower bound on the true body-only compute ratio (≈7.7×), not an upper bound."
findings.issue: The note says the FLOP proxy "overstates each model’s compute most for the smallest" and then says the proxy ratio (4.8×) is a "lower bound" on the true body-only ratio (≈7.7×). Those two statements are in tension: if the proxy overstates the smallest model’s compute more than the larger model’s, the proxy ratio should be biased downward, making 4.8× a lower bound — which is what the text says. But the preceding phrase "overstates each model’s compute most for the smallest" could be read as making the smallest model look artificially expensive, which would bias the ratio upward. The intended direction is correct but the prose is easy to misread.
findings.fix_instruction: Clarify: the proxy includes the embedding-table lookup as if it were per-position matmul; because MiniLM’s embedding table is a larger share of its total parameters, the proxy inflates MiniLM’s compute more than mpnet’s, so the proxy ratio (4.8×) understates the body-only compute ratio (≈7.7×). State the direction explicitly once and avoid the ambiguous "overstates most for the smallest" phrasing.
